activities.name: Mysore Palace – guided tour (marble corridors are stroller‑friendly and the palace opens early, perfect for a family with a 10‑year‑old)
Devaraja Market – short walk to explore local spices and silk (flat paths, good for a child to see colours and textures)

meals.breakfast: At hotel – soft idli with mild sambar (kid‑friendly, easy to chew)

lunch.description: plain rice with dal and carrot‑stir fry – near Devaraja Market (≈0.5 km from Palace)
lunch.location_note: near Devaraja Market — approx 0.5km from base

dinner.description: Mysore masala dosa – crisp, served with coconut chutney (local specialty)
Vegetable pulao with raita – mild flavors, sit‑down restaurant, child‑safe
Rooftop heritage restaurant – thali with ghee‑roasted veggies and mango lassi (premium ambience)

days.notes: Moderate pace; early evening dinner before 8 PM works well for the child. Watch out for auto‑rickshaw drivers who may divert you to commission‑based silk shops; insist on meter. Keep stroller handy for palace corridors, but be prepared to leave it at security for Durbar Hall.

activities.name: Karanji Lake – nature walk & bird‑watching (flat boardwalk, stroller‑friendly)
Boat ride on Karanji Lake (30 min gentle ride, great for the 10‑year‑old)

meals.breakfast: At hotel – soft poha with peanuts (easy to chew, kid‑friendly)

lunch.description: roti with paneer butter masala – near the lake entrance (≈0.2 km from parking)
lunch.location_note: near Karanji Lake entrance — approx 0.2km from base

dinner.description: Ragi mudde with sambar – traditional Karnataka comfort food (local)
Creamy pasta primavera – kid‑safe, served in a family‑friendly bistro
Fine‑dining terrace – set menu with Mysore wine pairing (premium ambience)

days.notes: Rain is possible in December; carry a light rain jacket. The lake area is flat and safe for the child. Snacks may be needed for the boat ride as on‑site stalls offer limited child‑appropriate meals.

activities.name: Chamundi Hill – temple visit via paved road (avoids the 1,008‑step climb, suitable for a 10‑year‑old)
Brindavan Gardens – evening fountain show (arrive early for a comfortable seat, child can enjoy lights and music)

meals.breakfast: At hotel – plain dosa with coconut chutney (soft, child‑friendly)

lunch.description: plain rice with mixed vegetable curry – near Chamundi Temple (≈5 km from city centre)
lunch.location_note: near Chamundi Temple — approx 5km from base

dinner.description: Mysore veg thali – includes soft rotis, rice, and dal (local comfort)
Cheese pizza with thin crust – sit‑down family restaurant, kid loves it
Royal Heritage dining room – candlelit thali with ghee‑roasted vegetables (premium ambience)

days.notes: Use a shared auto (₹60/seat) or private cab for Chamundi to avoid the steep steps. Carry snacks for the hilltop as stalls mainly sell vada/bajji. Book the Brindavan fountain show in advance; seats fill quickly. Evening temperatures drop to ~15 °C, so bring a light jacket.

activities.name: Srirangapatna Fort & Tipu Sultan’s Summer Palace – short walks, flat terrain (ideal for a 10‑year‑old)

meals.breakfast: At hotel – soft upma with grated carrots (easy to eat, child‑friendly)

lunch.description: plain rice with sambar and carrot sticks – near Srirangapatna Fort (≈2 km from railway station)
lunch.location_note: near Srirangapatna Fort — approx 2km from base

dinner.description: Mysore style vegetable korma with naan – local flavor
Mild butter paneer with jeera rice – family‑friendly, well‑cooked for the child
Premium riverside lounge – set menu with live music (premium ambience)

days.notes: Depart Mysore by evening Shatabdi. Keep an eye on train timings; booking ahead avoids last‑minute price hikes. The town is compact, so walking is easy for the child. Remember to carry water and a small snack for the train journey.

warnings: Auto‑rickshaw drivers in Mysore often divert tourists to commission‑based silk shops; always ask for the meter and state your exact destination.
Chamundi Hill’s 1,008‑step ascent is unsuitable for a child; use the flat paved road or shared auto to reach the temple.
Food stalls at Chamundi and Brindavan Gardens have limited child‑friendly meals; carry snacks and drinks for the 10‑year‑old.
December can bring light rain; pack a rain jacket and be ready to shift indoor activities if needed.
Booking the Brindavan fountain show in advance is essential as seats fill quickly, especially for families.

Auto drivers often divert tourists to private "government emporium" silk saree and sandalwood shops on commission – tell your auto driver the destination only; buy genuine Mysore silk at the KSIC showroom (Mananthody Road, near the Palace) and authentic sandalwood at the KS&DL retail outlet near Lalitha Mahal Road.

Station and palace‑area touts quote ₹800–1,500 for a "Chamundi + Brindavan package" – legitimate rates are Bus No. 201 to Chamundi Hills (₹25/person) and direct bus to Brindavan Gardens (₹35/person); a private cab booked via Ola costs ₹400–500 return, which is ₹100–150 cheaper than the touts.
The 1,008‑step ascent at Chamundi Hills is not suitable for young children; use the flat, paved road (shared auto ₹60/seat, private cab ₹300–400 return) instead.

Chamundi hilltop stalls and Brindavan Gardens canteen offer limited, overpriced food (vada, bajji, coffee ₹30–60; meals ₹100–150/plate) – neither location has child‑appropriate meals, so carry snacks from Mysore city.
Auto‑rickshaws within the city charge ₹50–120; most drivers use meters – insist on meter use to avoid overcharging.
Veg‑centric cuisine dominates; coconut is used in many chutneys and gravies – note this for any coconut allergies.

For toddlers and young kids, plain idli with mild sambar is available at all Udupi restaurants; Mysore Pak in small pieces is fine for children 2+. Carry familiar snacks for the 10‑year‑old if dining at hilltop stalls.
Stroller access is fine in the outer marble corridors of Mysore Palace and the flat paths of Karanji Lake, but the Durbar Hall requires depositing strollers at security; plan to keep the child close.
Musical fountain shows at Brindavan Gardens cost ₹90 per person (7 PM, 8 PM, 9 PM slots) and attract dense crowds – arrive early and sit at the outer edge for a comfortable view.
personalization_notes: Heritage focus: Palace, Chamundi Hill, and Srirangapatna align with your interest in history.
Food‑centric plan: each day features a kid‑safe dish and a local specialty, matching your food‑travel style.
Child‑friendly pacing: activities are limited to short walks or easy rides, keeping the 10‑year‑old engaged without fatigue.
